title: Rocco’s New Fridge Is Small Enough for Your Desk—and Costs $295
gist: Short promotional Wired Gear note: Rocco launched the Mini Mini, a $295 desktop version of its vintage-style beverage fridge, versus $1,999-plus for its full-size models. Specs are company claims; Wired had not tested it.

insights.claim: Rocco released the Mini Mini, a $295 countertop beverage fridge, as a low-priced entry point to a brand whose full-size fridges cost $1,999 and up.
insights.speaker: Kat Merck
insights.so_what: Premium appliance brands are adding sub-$300 entry SKUs to widen the funnel.
insights.locator: If you've always coveted Rocco’s vintage-inspired

insights.claim: Rocco claims the Mini Mini holds 12 standard 12-ounce cans and cools to 41 degrees Fahrenheit, with 360-degree ventilation and refrigeration mechanics underneath so it can sit flush against a wall; Wired had not tested these claims.
insights.speaker: Kat Merck
insights.so_what: Unverified spec claims; cooling performance is the differentiator in a category where small fridges typically run warm.
insights.quote: the first countertop fridge with real fridge standards.

insights.claim: Unlike Rocco's larger Classic and Essential fridges, the Mini Mini lacks the smart-beverage recognition feature, and buyers of a full-size Classic or Essential get $50 off the Mini Mini.
insights.speaker: Kat Merck
insights.so_what: Bundle discount suggests the Mini Mini is positioned as an add-on attach product.
